statement: The end comparison, including the exceptional types
depends_on: BBM2015 sphere theorem; augmented Teichmuller collar model
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: Let $2g-2+n>0$. Let $L_{g,n}$ be the boundary of the real oriented blow-up of the analytic Deligne--Mumford stack $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$, with corners rounded. The natural map \[ L_{g,n}\longrightarrow\mathcal M_{g,n}^{\rm an}\simeq B\Gamma_{g,n} \] has homotopy fibre $|\mathcal C_{g,n}|$. For nonempty boundary it induces an equivalence of fundamental groupoids precisely in the following ranges: \[ g=0,\ n\geq6;\qquad g=1,\ n\geq3;\qquad g\geq2,\ n\geq0. \] For $(0,5)$ and $(1,2)$ it induces a surjection on fundamental groups with kernel a free group of countably infinite rank. For $(0,4)$ and $(1,1)$ it does not induce a surjection on the fundamental group at a fixed boundary component. At $(0,3)$ the boundary is empty.

statement: Depth three is the sharp uniform input for the end's one-type
depends_on: D.1; normal-crossings simplex/torus model
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: In the normal-crossings link construction, retain every deployed stratum of depth at most $r$ and every flag among them. The resulting homotopy colimit maps naturally to the full link by an $(r-1)$-connected map. Thus depths $1,2,3$ compute its fundamental groupoid. Depths $1,2$ do not suffice uniformly: at the transverse meeting of three branches the fundamental groups are $\mathbb Z^4$ for the truncated diagram and $\mathbb Z^3$ for the full link. Applied to the stable moduli stack, this computes $\Pi_1(L_{g,n})$; D.1 gives precisely the types where it computes $\Pi_1(\mathcal M_{g,n})$. It does not compute $\Pi_1(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ by that identification.

statement: Compactification independence of the two end constructions
depends_on: BBT2013; valuative criterion for properness
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: For any compact Hausdorff compactification $U\subset X$ with $D=X\setminus U$, the archimedean punctured-neighborhood pro-space is canonically the end system $\{U\setminus K\}_{K\subset U\text{ compact}}$. For smooth proper normal-crossings pairs this pro-homotopy type is constant, with representative the rounded real-oriented-blow-up boundary. Over a trivially valued field $k$, a proper modification $X'\to X$ equal to the identity on $U$ induces an isomorphism \[ W(X',X'\setminus U)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }W(X,D),\qquad W(X,D)=X^{\beth}\setminus(U^{\beth}\cup D^{\beth}). \] For proper $X$, this space is $U^{\rm an}\setminus U^{\beth}$. Properness cannot be removed: the compactifications $\mathbb G_m\subset\mathbb A^1$ and $\mathbb G_m\subset\mathbb P^1$ give one and two punctured boundary tubes respectively.

notes: For the tripod, the archimedean end is three circles, the analytic open curve has homotopy type $S^1\vee S^1$, and the underlying trivially valued punctured tube is three open intervals. For $(\overline M_{0,5},D)$ the integral homology is free, with Betti numbers \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrr} &b_0&b_1&b_2&b_3\\\hline M_{0,5}^{\rm an}&1&5&6&0\\ L_{0,5}&1&11&11&1\\ W(\overline M_{0,5},D)&1&6&0&0. \end{array} \] The first comparison in D.1 sends every peripheral circle to its meridian. The nonarchimedean skeleton map sends a valuation to the normalized vector of its boundary orders, and retracts its underlying space onto the Petersen graph.

statement: The exact link calculation and a uniform rank-selection bound
depends_on: BBM2015 sphere theorem; exact cut-component join calculation
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: For a nonempty multicurve $\sigma$ let $v_0(\sigma)$ be the number of rational components after cutting. Then its upper link has homotopy type a wedge of spheres of dimension \[ H(\sigma)=2g-3+n-v_0(\sigma). \] A pair-of-pants factor is interpreted as the join unit $S^{-1}$. For $g\geq1$ and $0\leq k<d$, $|P_k|$ is at least \[ \left(\min\left\{h(g,n),\left\lfloor\frac{2(k+1)}3\right\rfloor\right\}-1\right)\text{-connected}. \] For $g=0$ it is $(k-1)$-connected. In every genus $P_1$ is connected and $P_2$ is simply connected, with the empty-multicurve convention at $k\geq d$.

statement: The original Lead 4 and the four requested computations
depends_on: D.5; BBM2015 sphere theorem
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: The original bound $(\min(k,2g-2+n)-1)$ is false: at $(g,n,k)=(2,1,3)$ the complex is a nontrivial wedge of two-spheres. The complete low-type table, with $\ast$ denoting a contractible cone and $\bigvee_\infty$ a countable wedge, is \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} (g,n)&d&P_1&P_2&P_3\\\hline (1,2)&2&\bigvee_\infty S^1&\ast&\ast\\ (1,3)&3&\bigvee_\infty S^1&\bigvee_\infty S^2&\ast\\ (2,0)&3&\bigvee_\infty S^1&\bigvee_\infty S^2&\ast\\ (2,1)&4&\bigvee_\infty S^1&\bigvee_\infty S^2&\bigvee_\infty S^2. \end{array} \] All $P_0$ are nonempty discrete sets; $P_k$ is contractible for $k\geq d$. The corrected proposed bound with $h(g,n)$ in place of $2g-2+n$ holds in all four rows.

statement: The corrected Lead 4 also fails, with an explicit retraction
depends_on: D.5; explicit forgetting retraction; BBM2015 sphere theorem
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: For every $g\geq1$, $n\geq2$, put $d=3g-3+n$ and $h=2g-3+n$. Then $P_{d-2}$ is exactly $(h-2)$-connected: its first possible nonzero reduced homology is in degree $h-1$, and that group contains a direct summand \[ \widetilde H_{h-1}(\mathcal C_{g,n-1};\mathbb Z) \cong\bigoplus_{\mathbb N}\mathbb Z. \] In particular, at $(g,n,k)=(2,2,3)$ one has $d=5$, $h=3$, and $P_3$ is simply connected with nonzero second homology. This refutes the corrected proposed $(\min(k,h)-1)$ bound. More generally the same counterexample family refutes it for every $g\geq2,n\geq2$ at $k=d-2$. D.5 is the uniform all-genus bound proved here.

statement: Good projective pairs are Mori hyperbolic and their comparisons are log crepant
depends_on: Svaldi2019 Theorem1.1; logarithmic Jacobian; negativity lemma
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: A good projective pair has no nonconstant algebraic map $\mathbb A^1\to S$ into any open stratum. For a simple normal-crossings boundary, $K_X+D$ is nef. For two such completions and a common smooth normal-crossings resolution $p:Z\to X$, $q:Z\to Y$, write $B=Z\setminus U$. Then \[ K_Z+B=p^*(K_X+D)+A_p=q^*(K_Y+E)+A_q, \qquad A_p=A_q\geq0. \] The common divisor is exceptional for both projections. A proper birational morphism between good smooth projective simple normal-crossings pairs, equal to the identity on $U$, is toroidal and log \'etale.

statement: All passports, cusp fields, Atkin--Lehner actions, and signatures
depends_on: CDH2014 Table2; RouseWebb2015 cusp theorem; d_lambencies.py

notes: For each lambency in Cheng--Duncan--Harvey's Table~2, the following tables give the complete permutation cover $X_0(N)\to X(1)$, its cusps, the action of the subgroup $S$ of exact divisors, and the signature of $\Gamma_0(N)+S$. The signature convention is $(0;e_2,e_3;c)$: genus zero, $e_i$ elliptic points of order $i$, and $c$ cusps. The genus $g_0$ in the first table is that of $X_0(N)$ before taking the $S$-quotient. A cycle expression $a^b$ means $b$ cycles of length $a$. These are signatures of the effective modular orbifold. The homomorphism $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)\to\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ has kernel $\{\pm I\}$, which acts trivially on every dart. Pulling the effective quotient back through this central extension restores the moduli stack of elliptic curves: its generic inertia is $\mu_2$ and its elliptic inertia orders are $4$ and $6$. Thus the displayed finite cover and its unrigidified modular stack are related by that specified central gerbe.

statement: The exact tripod comparison and the eta-product check
depends_on: D.14; Newman modularity and Ligozat divisor formulas; d_lambencies.py
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: The normalization of $X_0(N)\times_{X(1)}X(2)$ has one component of degree $\mu$ over $X(2)$ for odd $N$, and three components, each of degree $\mu/3$, for even $N$. They are defined over $\mathbb Q$. The component containing the standard cusp is isomorphic to $X_0(4N)$ for odd $N$ and to $X_0(2N)$ for even $N$; the other components differ by permutation of the three tripod punctures. For $4\mid N$ there is also the direct cover $X_0(N)\to X_0(4)$ of degree $\mu/6$. For all twenty-three rows the exact modular function $T^X=1/\eta_{\pi^X}$ is $S$-invariant and descends to a $\mathbb Q$-coordinate on $X_0(N)/S$, with a unique simple pole and expansion $q^{-1}-d^X+O(q)$. The attached computation supplies the full integral cusp divisor and coefficients through $q^{30}$. The assertions of genus zero and invariance follow from those exact divisors and modular transformation criteria, without an inference from a truncated series.

statement: Canonical reconstruction from the supplied face and collar diagram
depends_on: D.1; D_LabruereParis2001 Corollary2.11(i); coordinate angular quotient
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: Let $\mathcal V$ be the real oriented blow-up of a smooth complex normal-crossings Deligne--Mumford pair $(\mathcal X,\mathcal D)$, with its full deployed face diagram, collars, and maps to the strata. Collapsing precisely the normal angular circles over the zero radial coordinates recovers $\mathcal X$ as a topological stack. Equivalently, the mapping-cylinder pushout \[ \widehat X=X^*\mathop{\amalg}_{\dot X} C(p) \] of cote~150, scans~32--35, performed successively on the deployed strata, gives this same stack. For the supplied data, the final isomorphism is canonical and independent of the order of a compatible induction. For $\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}$, the fundamental groupoid is already that of the compactification after all open divisors have been attached to the open stratum. In the deepest-strata-first reconstruction starting from $\mathcal V$, it is already that groupoid after the first layer, consisting of all maximal-corner fibres. In both descriptions it is the connected simply connected groupoid. These are two explicitly related filtrations of the same final quotient.

statement: The corrected maquette and its comparison fibres
depends_on: D_CGP2021; D_CGPMarked2022; actual point-fibre action groupoids
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None; readings register preserves unused uncertainties
notes: Let $\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+}$ be the category of stable labelled graphs with at least one edge, with specified contractions and graph isomorphisms as morphisms. Define \[ \mathcal B_p= \{\,(G,\lambda):|E(G)|=p+1,\ \lambda:E(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{0,\ldots,p\}\,\}/\cong . \] Relabelling gives the symmetric-group action; an injection of label sets gives a face by contracting precisely the omitted edges. Then $\mathcal B$ is a symmetric semisimplicial set, its realization is the boundary complex, and the map assigning the label weights to the edge lengths is a homeomorphism \[ |\mathcal B|\xrightarrow{\sim}\Delta_{g,n}. \] Here $\Delta_{g,n}$ is the space of stable tropical curves of total finite-edge length one. The category with the automorphisms retained has the explicit comparison \[ B\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+}\simeq \operatorname*{hocolim}_{(\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+})^{\rm op}}\Delta_G \longrightarrow \operatorname*{colim}_{(\mathsf G_{g,n}^{+})^{\rm op}}\Delta_G =\Delta_{g,n},\qquad \Delta_G=\{(\ell_e)\geq0:\sum\ell_e=1\}. \] The actual point fibre of this homotopy-colimit model over a metric graph $(G,\ell)$ has homotopy type $B\operatorname{Aut}(G,\ell)$. The map need not be a quasifibration; this assertion concerns its actual point fibres. Adding the zero-edge graph makes the full graph category contractible, since that graph is terminal. The analytic boundary end has a compatible comparison to these models. Over a positive-length metric multicurve $(\sigma,\ell)$, the point fibre of its Borel-model map to $\Delta_{g,n}$ is $B\operatorname{Stab}_{\Gamma_{g,n}}(\sigma,\ell)$. The map of that fibre to the graph-model fibre is induced by the graph-action homomorphism, whose kernel is the node-framed pure cut-surface group. In particular its homotopy fibre is the classifying space of that kernel.
